papers.title: Understanding genetic determinants of bacterial adaptation to plant niches: Toward more robust bioinoculant design.
papers.abstract: Plant-associated bacteria offer a sustainable alternative to chemical inputs in agriculture, yet the field performance of microbial inoculants remains inconsistent. A central but frequently overlooked cause is that bioprospecting pipelines still select strains on the basis of plant-growth-promoting activities, while the bacterial genetic traits that determine whether a strain can reach, colonise and persist in a given root compartment are rarely assessed. Previous reviews have largely catalogued growth-promoting functions or described root microbiome assembly from the plant's perspective, here
papers.summary: This review argues that bioinoculant development pipelines focus too heavily on plant-growth-promoting traits while neglecting the bacterial genetic determinants of root colonization and persistence. The authors propose incorporating assessment of these colonization-related genetic traits into strain selection to improve the consistency of field performance.

papers.title: EsViritu is a sensitive and specific profiler for viral pathogen detection and genome recovery in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing allows for detection of any number of pathogenic viruses from a single sample without a priori knowledge of its contents. This has created a substantial opportunity to characterize pathogens in humans and their environment, but the field is held back by a lack of bioinformatics tools for taxonomic profiling and reconstructing virus genomes. The ideal profiler would simultaneously do two things: report viruses at single-read sensitivity so that ultra-low-abundance pathogens are not missed and hold near-perfect specificity so that a pathogen is never falsely reported. Here
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EsViritu is a new bioinformatics tool for detecting and reconstructing viral genomes from metagenomic sequencing data. It aims to achieve both single-read sensitivity (so even ultra-low-abundance viruses are detected) and near-perfect specificity (so no false positives are reported), addressing a key gap in viral pathogen profiling.

papers.title: Genome-resolved ecology and evolution of the microbiome enabled by quantitative long-read metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Standard metagenomics resolves microbial communities only in relative terms and at coarse taxonomic resolution, obscuring how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host. We present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a quantitative metagenomics platform coupling long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality genomes, including from degraded or low-input stool, and measure absolute, genome-resolved strain abundances. We validate LRQ using large plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense sampling fro
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a metagenomics platform that combines long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality genomes and measure absolute, genome-resolved strain abundances, even from degraded or low-input stool. They validate the method with plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense longitudinal sampling to track how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host.

papers.title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
papers.abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. Results: The results showed that heat-inactivated PC-01 significantly decreased the Disease Activity Index and H&E histopathological scores (p < 0.05). It also reduced the serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokin
papers.summary: In a DSS-induced mouse model of colitis, heat-inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 reduced disease activity and histopathological damage and lowered serum pro-inflammatory cytokines. The protective effect appears to be mediated through modulation of the gut microbiota and improvement of intestinal barrier function.

papers.title: Probiotics as a Barrier Against Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli in Contaminated Rice-Protein-Based Infant Formulas.
papers.abstract: Background/Aims: The presence of pathogens such as Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli in infant formulas, even at concentrations below the detection threshold, poses a health risk. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to limit pathogen proliferation. This study evaluated two probiotic strains (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 and Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis IM-1) to inhibit the growth of these pathogens under simulated conditions. Methods: Assays were conducted using reconstituted infant formula supplemented or not with the probiotics combination and challenged with E
papers.summary: This study tested whether two probiotic strains (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus HN001 and Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis IM-1) could inhibit Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli growth in reconstituted rice-protein-based infant formula. The probiotics were assessed under simulated conditions to determine their potential as a barrier against pathogen proliferation in contaminated formulas. The work evaluates a practical food-safety intervention for infant formula.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of developmental-category-associated fungal communities in the gut contents of Achatina fulica, an intermediate host of Angiostrongylus cantonensis.
papers.abstract: The invasive giant African snail (Achatina fulica) poses serious agricultural and ecological threats and serves as an important intermediate host of the zoonotic parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, which causes human eosinophilic meningitis. While its gut bacterial microbiome has been extensively characterized, the gut mycobiome remains largely uncharacterized. In particular, variations in gut fungal communities across developmental stages remain unknown, limiting our understanding of the A. fulica gut holobiont.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the fungal communities (mycobiome) in the gut contents of the giant African snail Achatina fulica, an invasive species and intermediate host for the parasite that causes human eosinophilic meningitis. The authors compare fungal community composition across different developmental stages of the snail, addressing a gap since the gut bacterial microbiome had been well studied but the mycobiome was largely unknown. The work provides a baseline description of stage-associated fungal diversity in this host.

papers.title: From Prediction to Mechanism: Explainable AI for Plant-Microbiome Multi-Omics Integration and Biological Discovery.
papers.abstract: Predicting complex phenotypes from plant-microbiome multi-omics data has advanced significantly with machine learning and deep learning. However, traditional black-box models remain limited by their focus on predictive performance rather than mechanistic biological understanding. To bridge this gap, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a key framework to transform biological data analysis from correlation mapping to hypothesis-driven discovery. This review synthesizes current advances in XAI methodologies, including post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically
papers.summary: This review synthesizes explainable AI (XAI) approaches for integrating plant-microbiome multi-omics data, arguing that black-box predictive models must be complemented by interpretability methods to move from correlation to mechanistic insight. It surveys post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically interpretable models, framing XAI as a bridge between prediction and hypothesis-driven biological discovery.

papers.title: Comparative Shotgun Metagenomics of Microbial Communities Associated with Two Geothermal Systems in Kazakhstan.
papers.abstract: Geothermal-associated microbial communities remain poorly characterized in Central Asia. Here, shotgun metagenomics was used to compare microbial communities associated with thermally influenced substrates from the Chundzha and Rakhman geothermal systems in Kazakhstan. Six metagenomes representing three spatial replicates per site yielded approximately 6.5-7.3 Gb of clean sequence data per sample. Species-level richness showed a directional trend toward higher values in Chundzha, whereas Shannon diversity was similar between sites. Genus-level Bray-Curtis ordination showed apparent site-associ
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare microbial communities from two understudied geothermal systems in Kazakhstan, Chundzha and Rakhman. They found a directional trend toward higher species richness at Chundzha, while Shannon diversity was similar between sites, and genus-level ordination showed apparent site-associated community differences. The work provides baseline metagenomic data for Central Asian geothermal microbiomes.

papers.title: Feeder- and Drinker-Associated Microbiota Differ from Host-Associated Fecal Microbiota During a Commercial Broiler Production Cycle with Age-Associated Changes in Taxonomic Composition.
papers.abstract: Broiler chickens are continuously exposed to microorganisms in the production environment, but the relationship between microorganisms on bird-contact surfaces and fecal microbiota remains unclear. In this exploratory observational study, shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to compare microbial communities in feeder- and drinker-associated surface samples and individual fecal samples during one production cycle in a single commercial system housing Ross 308 broilers. The dataset comprised 22 individual fecal samples collected on days 1, 7, 19, 27, and 39 and four composite feeder- or drink
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This exploratory study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare microbial communities on feeder and drinker surfaces with individual fecal samples from commercial broiler chickens across a production cycle. The researchers found that feeder- and drinker-associated microbiota differ compositionally from host-associated fecal microbiota, and that taxonomic composition shifts with bird age. The findings suggest that environmental surface communities are not simply mirrors of gut microbiota, which has implications for understanding how production environments shape bird health.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota Signatures Associated with Metastatic Prostatic Cancer Treated with Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitor (ARPI) Therapy.
papers.abstract: Metastatic prostate cancer (MPCa) remains an aggressive disease despite the introduction of androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs), and biomarkers predicting progression are still lacking. The aim of this study was to investigate gut microbiota (GM) composition and functional potential associated with advanced disease and progression under ARPI therapy. The GM of 15 patients with metastatic PCa receiving ARPIs, including 5 patients with disease progression, was compared with that of 39 patients with untreated (UT) PCa using shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The metastatic PCa cohor
papers.summary: This study compared the gut microbiota of 15 metastatic prostate cancer patients receiving androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) with 39 untreated prostate cancer patients using shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The authors identified distinct microbial composition and functional signatures associated with metastatic disease and with progression on ARPI therapy, suggesting the gut microbiome may serve as a biomarker for treatment response. The small sample size (only 5 progressors) limits the strength of these associations.

papers.title: Recovering anaerobic bacterial genomes in saliva, tumour and blood whole genome sequencing data from patients with prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Microbial constituents in the gastrointestinal tract, the urine and prostate tissue are being linked with clinical differences in prostate cancer, and a recent meta-analysis has linked periodontal disease to this cancer. Several hypotheses exist regarding how specific bacteria can contribute towards the development of prostate cancer. Recovering microbial genomes, and their genomic features, from clinical samples and investigating fine-scale taxonomy is a critical first step in investigating causality. Here, we describe the microbial diversity of samples associated with prostate cancer. Metage
papers.summary: This study recovered anaerobic bacterial genomes from whole-genome sequencing data of saliva, tumour, and blood samples from prostate cancer patients, characterizing the microbial diversity associated with the disease. It provides a fine-scale taxonomic view of microbial constituents in these clinical samples, which is a necessary step toward investigating whether specific bacteria contribute to prostate cancer development.

papers.title: Protocol for mixed methods study exploring the gut-brain health among South Indian population.
papers.summary: This protocol outlines a mixed-methods study designed to investigate gut-brain health interactions within a South Indian population. It combines quantitative and qualitative approaches to explore how gut microbiome composition relates to neurological and psychological health outcomes in this understudied group. The work aims to establish a culturally tailored framework for future gut-brain axis research in South Asia.

papers.title: A gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking.
papers.summary: This study constructs an integrated score combining gut microbiota composition, microbial metabolites, and host gene expression to subtype rheumatoid arthritis patients and predict their response to treatment. The authors validate key microbial-metabolite-host gene relationships using in silico knockout simulations. The resulting score stratifies RA patients into distinct subtypes with differing therapeutic outcomes.

papers.title: An optimized flow cytometry sorting-sequencing workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction bias in sorted microbial communities.
papers.abstract: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) followed by metataxonomics is commonly used to probe the composition of microbial subpopulations with a functionality of interest. Metataxonomic analysis of sorted low-microbial-biomass samples is prone to contamination and bias introduced during sorting and DNA extraction. To improve metataxonomic accuracy, the DNA yield obtained by the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit was first maximized. FACS-sequencing using the optimized DNA extraction method distorted the composition of sorted microbiota by introducing sheath fluid contaminants, termed the FACSome. Sinc
papers.summary: This study optimizes a FACS-to-sequencing workflow for low-biomass sorted microbial communities, first maximizing DNA yield from the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit and then identifying a previously unrecognized bias: sheath fluid contaminants (the 'FACSome') that distort sorted community composition. The optimized workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction biases, improving metataxonomic accuracy for sorted subpopulations.

papers.title: DNAharvester: A Nextflow Pipeline for Analysing Highly Degraded DNA from Ancient and Historical Specimens.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences.
papers.summary: DNAharvester is a Nextflow pipeline designed to process highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens, addressing challenges like short fragments, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and contamination. It aims to reduce spurious mapping and reference bias, improving the reliability of downstream population genetic analyses for aDNA studies.

papers.title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA.
papers.abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. Notably, microbial community str
papers.summary: This study used sedimentary ancient DNA and stable isotope analysis from a lake sediment core in northern China to reconstruct how microbial communities responded to environmental change over centuries. Microbial community assembly was mainly deterministic, but stochastic processes increased sharply after 1850, coinciding with the end of the Little Ice Age and intensified human activity. The work shows that lake microbial structure and function shifted in response to both climatic and anthropogenic forcing.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, sleep and coronary artery disease: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Inadequate and poor-quality sleep is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Gut microbiota may play a role in sleep regulation. However, the associations between gut microbiota, sleep, and CAD risk, and the causal nature of these associations, remain unclear. We performed a 2-step Mendelian randomization analysis using summary-level data to assess the association between gut microbiota and CAD and the potential mediating roles of sleep-related traits (i.e., chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short sleep, and long sleep) herein. The inverse-variance weigh
papers.summary: This study used two-step Mendelian randomization with summary-level genetic data to test whether gut microbiota influence coronary artery disease risk and whether sleep traits mediate this relationship. The analysis examined multiple sleep-related traits (chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short and long sleep) as potential mediators between gut microbiota and CAD. The abstract is truncated, so specific causal estimates and mediation proportions are not available, but the work applies a causal-inference framework to a tripartite microbiome-sleep-cardiovascular question.

papers.title: Causal relationship between oral microbiome, circulating inflammatory proteins and lung cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Recent research showed that oral microbiomes (OMs), as the main source of lung microbiomes, were associated with lung cancer (LC), but the causal relationship and mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the immune mechanisms of LC through the "OM - inflammatory proteins - LC" axis. Instrumental variables covering 43 oral microbial taxa, 91 circulating inflammatory proteins, and LC subtypes were obtained from large-scale genome-wide association study summary data of European origin. We employed Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to validate causal links between the OM and LC a
papers.summary: Using Mendelian randomization on European GWAS summary data, the authors tested whether 43 oral microbial taxa causally influence lung cancer subtypes, and whether 91 circulating inflammatory proteins mediate this relationship along an 'oral microbiome–inflammatory proteins–lung cancer' axis. The study aims to clarify immune mechanisms linking oral microbes to lung cancer risk.

papers.title: Development of a novel diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia based on microbial community characteristics.
papers.abstract: The lung microbiota plays a key role in pneumonia. A correct diagnosis in the early stage helps treatment and limits severity progression of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).
papers.journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
papers.summary: This study develops a diagnostic tool for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) by analyzing the composition of the lung microbiome. The authors likely identify microbial community signatures that distinguish CAP patients from controls, offering a potential early diagnostic approach. The work highlights the diagnostic value of lung microbiota profiling.

papers.title: Transmission of lactic acid bacteria: a case study of the human vaginal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are among the microorganisms to which humans are most frequently exposed, largely via consumption of fermented foods and probiotics and through interpersonal contact. Such continued exposure to LAB does not necessarily result in stable engraftment, raising fundamental questions about which factors mediate successful LAB transmission and niche specialization across human-associated microbiomes. Here, we rethink transmission of LAB across the human life course, spanning food-associated, within-host, and interindividual routes, highlighting that LAB transfer can occur a
papers.summary: This review reconsiders how lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are transmitted between humans and across body sites, using the vaginal microbiome as a case study. It argues that despite frequent exposure through food, probiotics, and interpersonal contact, stable engraftment is not guaranteed, and it calls for a framework that integrates food-associated, within-host, and interindividual transmission routes across the human life course. The paper highlights open questions about which factors determine successful LAB transmission and niche specialization.

papers.title: MIMEco: multi-objective metabolic modeling to predict and explain pairwise interactions.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models provide a mechanistic framework for quantitatively exploring an organism's physiology and its interactions with the environment. However, their use in microbial community modeling has been limited since it usually relies on community-wide objective functions or the integration of community abundance data. Nevertheless, predicting microbial interactions is crucial for understanding ecosystem dynamics and thus requires dedicated methods. Here, we introduce Metabolic Interaction Modeling in Ecosystems (MIMEco), an open-source Python package that predicts pairwise mic
papers.summary: MIMEco is an open-source Python package that uses genome-scale metabolic models to predict pairwise microbial interactions without relying on community-wide objective functions or abundance data. It employs a multi-objective optimization approach to mechanistically explain how metabolic exchanges drive these interactions. This provides a dedicated tool for modeling microbial community dynamics.

papers.title: Oral Actinomyces Species Exposure is Associated with Anxiety-Like Behavior, Mitochondrial Remodeling, and Altered GABAergic Pathways.
papers.abstract: The human oral microbiome is increasingly recognized as a contributor to brain health, yet its mechanisms remain unclear. We previously found an enrichment of oral Actinomyces species in chronic cannabis smokers.
papers.summary: This study reports that oral exposure to Actinomyces species is associated with anxiety-like behavior in an animal model, accompanied by mitochondrial remodeling and changes in GABAergic signaling pathways. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between specific oral bacteria and brain function, potentially relevant to stress-related disorders.

papers.title: mums2: an R package for database-dependent and -independent analysis of untargeted metabolomics data.
papers.abstract: mums2 is an open-source R package that enables users to analyze data from untargeted metabolomics analyses. mums2 provides features that parallel existing tools for analyzing 16S rRNA gene sequence data, including data curation, annotation, clustering of features into operational metabolomic units (OMUs), and analyses based on ecological metrics.
papers.summary: mums2 is an open-source R package for analyzing untargeted metabolomics data, offering both database-dependent and database-independent workflows. It mirrors common 16S rRNA amplicon analysis tools, providing data curation, feature annotation, clustering into operational metabolomic units (OMUs), and ecological metric analyses. This gives microbiologists and metabolomics researchers a familiar, integrated framework for processing and interpreting untargeted metabolomics data.

papers.title: Optimized approaches to profile low biomass DNA and RNA virome in the upper respiratory tract of beef cattle.
papers.abstract: Viruses play a key role in cattle respiratory tract (RT) health, yet, profiling the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome (DNA and RNA viruses) from deep nasopharyngeal swabs (DNS) remains challenging due to their low biomass, lack of well-defined enrichment approaches, and a high proportion of unclassified viral sequences. This study aimed to optimize DNS preservation, nucleic acid extraction, and bioinformatics pipelines to enhance URT virome characterization in beef calves.
papers.summary: This study optimizes methods for characterizing the DNA and RNA virome of the upper respiratory tract in beef cattle, addressing challenges of low biomass and unclassified viral sequences. The authors systematically test preservation, extraction, and bioinformatics pipelines to improve virome profiling from deep nasopharyngeal swabs. The result is a refined workflow that enhances detection and classification of viruses in this understudied niche.

papers.title: Integrated In Silico Analysis Reveals ABC Transporter ATP-Binding Protein as a Therapeutic Target in Helicobacter pylori.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori remains a major cause of gastric diseases, while increasing antimicrobial resistance highlights the need for novel therapeutic targets. Here, we developed a comprehensive computational target-prioritization framework integrating Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify pathogen-specific drug targets in H. pylori J99. Twelve conserved domain families comprising 746 proteins were identified, and domain abundance showed a weak negative correlation with versatility
papers.summary: This study presents a computational pipeline combining Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to prioritize drug targets in Helicobacter pylori J99. The authors identify an ABC transporter ATP-binding protein as a pathogen-specific therapeutic candidate, addressing the need for new targets given rising antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Synergistic effect of gastric microbiome and host genetic factor predispose to gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Complex interaction between host genetic and environmental factors has a role in Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori)-related gastric tumorigenesis, while involvement of non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome may be also relevant to this process. We aimed to evaluate whether combining the non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome signatures and the gastric cancer (GC) predisposing genetic factors (PSCA rs2294008 and MUC1 rs4072037 polymorphisms) stratify a high GC risk subpopulation in a Japanese cohort.
papers.summary: This study examines whether combining non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome signatures with two known gastric cancer risk polymorphisms (PSCA rs2294008 and MUC1 rs4072037) can identify a high-risk subpopulation for gastric cancer in a Japanese cohort. The findings suggest that the gastric microbiome and host genetic factors act synergistically to predispose individuals to gastric cancer, potentially enabling better risk stratification beyond H. pylori status alone.

papers.title: A high-throughput pipeline for isolation and screening of the citrus bacteriome identifies Pseudomonas chlororaphis with anti-Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus activity.
papers.abstract: Plant microbiomes are a rich source of secondary metabolites, often with pathogen- or disease-suppressive traits. Huanglongbing (HLB) is a serious disease of citrus for which there is currently no cure. Here, we tested the hypothesis that bacteria native to the citrus microbiome may possess inhibitory activity against the associated causal agent of HLB, Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas). We coupled a robotic microfluidic isolation platform with a high-throughput antimicrobial screening assay using Liberibacter crescens, a culturable surrogate for the unculturable CLas, to identify isola
papers.summary: The authors developed a robotic microfluidic pipeline to isolate bacteria from the citrus microbiome and screened them for activity against Liberibacter crescens, a culturable surrogate for the unculturable HLB pathogen Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus. They identified Pseudomonas chlororaphis isolates with anti-CLas activity, suggesting native citrus bacteria could be a source of biocontrol agents against Huanglongbing.

papers.title: Inverse probability weighting-based mediation analysis for microbiome data.
papers.abstract: Mediation analysis is an important tool for elucidating causal mechanisms in biomedical research and has recently gained increasing attention in microbiome studies. Motivated by a microbiome study of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, we investigate whether the effect of induction chemotherapy intensity on infection status is mediated through gut microbial taxa. This problem poses substantial methodological challenges due to the high dimensionality, zero inflation, and dependence of microbial mediators, as well as the presence of an exposure-induced mediator-outcome confounder, antibiotic
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new statistical method for mediation analysis in microbiome studies, using inverse probability weighting to handle high-dimensional, zero-inflated, and correlated microbial taxa while accounting for exposure-induced confounding. Motivated by an AML study, it tests whether the effect of chemotherapy intensity on infection is mediated through gut microbes. The approach provides a rigorous causal framework for microbiome mediation questions.

papers.title: FAMUS: A Few-Shot Learning Framework for Large-Scale Protein Annotation.
papers.abstract: Gene function prediction is pivotal in genomic and metagenomic data analysis. Current annotation tools typically rely on the most similar sequence from the query database and struggle to robustly set meaningful hit thresholds, causing a major challenge for reliable annotation.
papers.summary: FAMUS introduces a few-shot learning framework for large-scale protein function annotation that moves beyond relying on the single most similar sequence and arbitrary hit thresholds. By learning from a small number of labeled examples, it aims to provide more robust and reliable gene function predictions for genomic and metagenomic data.

papers.title: A global atlas of the gut virome reveals subtype-specific and functional alterations in irritable bowel syndrome.
papers.abstract: The gut virome is a critical component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis; however, its role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains poorly understood due to limited sample sizes and geographic bias. We aimed to construct a comprehensive global atlas of the IBS gut virome to elucidate its composition, functional potential, and clinical relevance across diverse populations and IBS subtypes. We integrated multi-cohort data comprising 1,104 samples (790 IBS patients and 314 healthy controls) from 11 cohorts across 10 geographic regions. A standardized bioinformatic pipeline was employed to perfor
papers.summary: This study integrates gut virome data from 1,104 samples across 11 cohorts and 10 geographic regions to build a global atlas of the gut virome in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Using a standardized bioinformatic pipeline, the authors identify subtype-specific and functional alterations in the virome associated with IBS, highlighting its potential role in the microbiome-gut-brain axis. The work addresses prior limitations of small sample sizes and geographic bias, providing a broader view of virome involvement in IBS.

papers.title: Identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction.
papers.abstract: It is common to build predictive models for complex phenotypes, such as diseases, where sample sizes are often limited by the cost of data collection. Machine learning and statistical methods are widely used in these cases. However, they may fail to identify high-quality features and lead to suboptimal models with high underfitting or overfitting risks. Here, we present mBoost to identify low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction. Importantly, it provides confidence on model performance, helping researchers avoid the frustrating cycle of model switching for pos
papers.summary: The authors present mBoost, a tool that identifies low-quality features and suboptimal predictive models for complex phenotypes, addressing the common problem of overfitting or underfitting when sample sizes are limited. By flagging problematic features and providing confidence estimates on model performance, mBoost helps researchers avoid repeatedly switching models in search of better results. This work aims to improve the reliability of phenotype prediction in settings like disease modeling where data collection is costly.

papers.title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal s
papers.summary: This study performed functional metagenomic analysis on fecal samples from a prior randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the fungal nutraceutical Micodigest® in colorectal cancer surgery patients. While the original trial showed favorable taxonomic and inflammatory changes, this follow-up work reveals that the supplement also modifies the functional potential of the gut microbiome, moving beyond simple taxonomic shifts to identify changes in microbial gene content and metabolic pathways.

papers.title: Deciphering the heterogeneity of prodromal α-synucleinopathy: linking brain biotyping and gut dysbiosis in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated/idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a specific prodrome of α-synucleinopathies. We previously identified two distinct clinical-neuroimaging biotypes in iRBD: Biotype 1, marked by widespread cortical-subcortical-cerebellar atrophy with motor and cognitive deficits, and Biotype 2, with preserved brain structure and neurocognition. Converging evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in early α-synucleinopathy, yet its role in these divergent iRBD phenotypes remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study examines whether the two previously identified brain biotypes of isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) — one with widespread brain atrophy and cognitive/motor deficits, the other with preserved brain structure — differ in gut microbiome composition. By linking brain biotyping to gut dysbiosis, the authors aim to show that gut-brain axis involvement varies across prodromal α-synucleinopathy phenotypes, potentially explaining divergent trajectories toward Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies.

papers.title: Reduced-Complexity Cultivation of Human Oral Anaerobic Bacteria Using a Microdroplet-Based Culturomics Platform.
papers.abstract: The human oral microbiota contains fastidious anaerobes that remain uncultivated due to resource competition and overgrowth by dominant species in conventional plating. Culturomics approaches leveraging droplet-based microfluidics offer an alternative by physically compartmentalizing microbial cells. We established a polydimethylsiloxane-based microdroplet platform to isolate anaerobic bacteria from human oral rinse samples. Droplet generation conditions were optimized using fluorescent beads, and bacterial loading at the collection-drop level was evaluated using Escherichia coli. Two downstre
papers.summary: The authors developed a PDMS-based microdroplet platform to culture fastidious anaerobic bacteria from human oral rinse samples, using physical compartmentalization to reduce competition and overgrowth by dominant species. They optimized droplet generation with fluorescent beads and evaluated bacterial loading using E. coli, demonstrating a reduced-complexity culturomics approach for accessing previously uncultivated oral anaerobes.

papers.title: Early-Life Gut Microbiota and the Pediatric Gut-Lung Axis: A Systematic Review of Clinical, Preclinical, and Mechanistic Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The early-life gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in immune maturation and may influence respiratory health through the gut-lung axis. However, evidence linking microbial development, dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions to pediatric respiratory outcomes remains heterogeneous. This systematic review aimed to synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence on the pediatric gut-lung axis and its underlying mechanisms. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD4202510
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on how the early-life gut microbiota influences pediatric respiratory health via the gut-lung axis. It examines links between microbial development, dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions, while highlighting the heterogeneity of existing evidence. The review provides a structured overview of mechanistic pathways and identifies gaps for future research.

papers.title: Use of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing to Investigate Respiratory Pathogens in Influenza-Negative Nasopharyngeal Swabs From Cameroon's National Influenza Surveillance.
papers.abstract: In Cameroon, national influenza surveillance identifies influenza-positive cases, but the causes of non-influenza ARIs remain poorly characterized. We applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate respiratory pathogens in influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected through national influenza surveillance.
papers.summary: This study applies metagenomic next-generation sequencing to influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected through Cameroon's national influenza surveillance system, aiming to identify non-influenza respiratory pathogens causing acute respiratory infections. The work addresses a gap in understanding the etiology of non-influenza ARIs in Cameroon, where surveillance has focused primarily on influenza detection.

papers.title: Patterns of Functional Redundancy and Anaerobic Metabolic Potential Characterise the Skin Microbiome of a Critically Endangered Sawfish.
papers.abstract: Using shotgun metagenomics of largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis) skin and paired pool water samples, we provide the first taxonomic and functional characterisation of a sawfish skin microbiome and assess its ecological distinctiveness, assembly, and resilience relative to the surrounding water column. The skin microbiome was strongly host-associated and compositionally distinct, with lower taxonomic richness than the water column but dominated by Bacillota, particularly spore-forming Bacilli. Functional profiling revealed genes associated with sporulation, dormancy, anaerobic metabolism, and
papers.summary: This study provides the first taxonomic and functional characterization of the skin microbiome of the critically endangered largetooth sawfish using shotgun metagenomics. The skin microbiome is strongly host-associated and distinct from the surrounding water, dominated by spore-forming Bacillota, and enriched for genes involved in sporulation, dormancy, and anaerobic metabolism, suggesting functional redundancy and resilience strategies.

papers.title: Subclinical Mastitis and Antibiotic Exposure Reshape the Milk Bacteriome, Resistome, and Metabolic Functional Profiles in Dairy Cows.
papers.abstract: Subclinical mastitis (SCM) reduces milk yield and promotes antibiotic use, contributing to antimicrobial resistance. However, information on milk microbiome dysbiosis and resistome alterations in dairy cows remains limited. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 30 milk samples from 20 cows classified as SCM (n = 10), antibiotic-treated (ANT; n = 10), and healthy milk (HM; n = 10). Bacteriome, resistome, and metabolic functions were analyzed using bioinformatic tools. Microbial alpha diversity was significantly higher in HM than SCM and ANT samples (p < 0.05), with the greatest richnes
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of milk from dairy cows showed that both subclinical mastitis and antibiotic treatment reduce microbial diversity compared with healthy milk, and reshape the bacteriome, antibiotic resistance gene (resistome) content, and metabolic functional profiles. The study links mastitis-driven dysbiosis and antibiotic exposure to altered resistance potential in the milk microbiome.

papers.title: Genotype-dependent phosphorus acquisition responses of two soybean genotypes under combined low phosphorus and salt stress: evidence from root traits, exudates and rhizosphere microbiome.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization and phosphorus (P) deficiency often co-occur in coastal saline-alkali soils, severely limiting crop productivity. Although root exudates are known to mediate rhizosphere microbiome assembly, the coordinated associations among root exudates, rhizosphere microbes, and P acquisition under combined salinity stress and phosphate deficiency remain unclear. In this study, we used two salt-tolerant soybean genotypes differing in P efficiency (A74, P-efficient; A6, P-inefficient) as materials. In a controlled pot experiment, four treatments were established: control (CK), low P (LP),
papers.summary: This study compares two salt-tolerant soybean genotypes that differ in phosphorus-use efficiency (A74 efficient, A6 inefficient) grown under combined low-phosphorus and salt stress, examining root traits, root exudates, and rhizosphere microbiome composition. The work links genotype-specific root exudate profiles to rhizosphere microbial community assembly and phosphorus acquisition outcomes, suggesting coordinated root-exudate-microbe interactions underlie differential P efficiency under stress.

papers.title: Goat and cow milk merits distinct nutritional and functional properties based on simulated gastrointestinal digestion of infant.
papers.abstract: The nutritional and functional properties of goat and cow milk in digestive tract of infant is unclear. Applying simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion method, this study aims to systematically compare digestibility, peptide profiling, and immunomodulatory role of goat and cow milk, and further characterize their role in regulating homeostasis of gut microbiota and metabolism. It's found that the degree of hydrolysis and number of detected peptides was higher in goat milk (GM), while the relative abundance of predicted allergic peptides was higher in cow milk (CM). In addition, the expres
papers.summary: Using a simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion model, the authors compared goat and cow milk and found that goat milk was digested more extensively, producing more peptides, while cow milk contained a higher relative abundance of predicted allergenic peptides. They further examined how each milk type influenced gut microbiota and metabolic homeostasis, suggesting distinct nutritional and functional properties relevant to infant feeding.

papers.title: A high-resolution spatial model of the primate gut microbiome defines niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of the gastrointestinal microbiome is shaped by strong physicochemical gradients along the gut, yet many region-associated microbial niches remain poorly resolved in humans. Here, we used the rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) as a spatially resolved primate model to profile 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and targeted bile acid metabolomics, complemented by comparative human datasets. Microbial communities exhibited strong spatial stratification along the gastrointestinal tract, while host
papers.summary: This study maps the gut microbiome of rhesus macaques at high spatial resolution, profiling 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and bile acid metabolomics. The authors show that microbial communities are strongly stratified along the gut and identify niche-specific functions and host-adapted metabolic features, with comparisons to human datasets. The work provides a spatially resolved primate model for understanding region-specific microbial niches that remain poorly characterized in humans.

papers.title: Biases in high throughput sequencing methods affect microbial molecular ecology networks and keystone taxa identification in the Cinnamomum migao rhizosphere and phyllosphere.
papers.abstract: The rhizosphere and phyllosphere microbial symbiotic interactions are crucial factors affecting plant health and productivity. How to authentically reflect the species interactions and assembly processes that shape shaping microbial communities has attracted extensive attention from ecologists. The construction of most microbial networks relies on amplicon sequencing data, neglecting both total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions. The impacts of sequencing resolution ratio, microbial domain, and quantification methods on microbial interspecies interactions and network parameters st
papers.summary: This study examines how biases inherent in high-throughput sequencing methods—such as resolution limits and the omission of total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions—distort the construction of microbial co-occurrence networks and the identification of keystone taxa in the rhizosphere and phyllosphere of Cinnamomum migao. By comparing network parameters across sequencing resolutions, microbial domains, and quantification approaches, the authors show that these methodological choices can substantially alter inferred species interactions and assembly processes. The work highlights the need for more careful, standardized network construction to avoid misleading ecological conclusions.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups.
papers.summary: This study compares the pulmonary microbiome of patients with drug-sensitive versus multidrug-resistant tuberculosis using metagenomic sequencing. It identifies microbial community differences between the two groups, suggesting the lung microbiota may differ by drug-resistance status. The work provides a foundation for exploring whether microbiome features relate to TB pathogenesis or resistance.

papers.title: TSLC: differential abundance analysis method for identifying biologically relevant known microbes.
papers.abstract: Identifying biologically relevant microbes is a crucial task in human microbiome studies. Numerous computational and statistical methods have been proposed for this task. However, most existing methods are based solely on taxonomic information, even when whole-metagenome sequencing data are available, and thus cannot account for the fact that different microbes can perform the same or similar functions (known as functional redundancy) and for the contribution of unknown microbes to functional abundance. Hence, the identified differentially abundant microbes might not be biologically relevant t
papers.summary: The paper introduces TSLC, a differential abundance analysis method for microbiome studies that incorporates functional information from whole-metagenome sequencing data rather than relying only on taxonomic profiles. This allows it to account for functional redundancy among known microbes and the contribution of unknown microbes, aiming to identify microbes that are more biologically relevant. The abstract is truncated, so full validation results are not described.

papers.title: Effects of cultivation of herbaceous perennials on soil microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impacts of cultivating different herbaceous perennials on the rhizosphere microenvironment, nitrogen-cycling microbial communities, and functional genes in black soils of urban green spaces in Northeast China, thereby providing a scientific basis for rational urban plant configuration and interspecific differences in soil nutrient cycling. Focusing on five commonly utilized herbaceous perennials in Changchun (Lycopus lucidus [P-LL], Salvia japonica [P-SJ], Hemerocallis fulva [P-HF], Hosta ensata [P-HE], and Pseudolysimachion spicatum [P-PS]), this study integr
papers.summary: The study compares how five herbaceous perennial species grown in urban green spaces in Northeast China affect rhizosphere soil microbial communities and nitrogen-cycling functional genes. It finds that plant species identity shapes microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling potential in black soils, supporting species-specific plant configuration for urban landscaping.

papers.title: Metagenomic profiling reveals that divergent fire-adaptive strategies drive distinct fungal succession in pine litter decomposition.
papers.abstract: Decomposing litter is a critical driver of fuel bed formation and forest fire regimes, yet how divergent plant fire-adaptive strategies influence litter chemistry and subsequent fungal decomposition dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 6-month reciprocal litterbag experiment by incubating litter from two contrasting pine species-the fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis and the fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola-in both their own native habitat and that of the other species, coupled with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession and lignocellulolytic functional profiles
papers.summary: This study used a reciprocal litterbag experiment with two pine species that have contrasting fire-adaptive strategies (fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis vs. fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola) combined with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession during litter decomposition. The authors show that the divergent fire-adaptive strategies of the host plants drive distinct fungal community succession and lignocellulolytic functional profiles, linking plant fire traits to decomposer dynamics and fuel bed formation.

papers.title: Beyond community state types: vaginal microbial diversity and CST-IV signatures are associated with pregnancy in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.abstract: Despite significant progress in assisted reproductive technology, in vitro fertilization (IVF) pregnancy rates remain suboptimal. Although the vaginal microbiome has been implicated in IVF outcomes, prior studies often overlooked embryonic aneuploidy, a major confounder. This study aimed to investigate the association between the vaginal microbiome and pregnancy outcomes in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.summary: This study examined whether vaginal microbiome composition is linked to pregnancy success in IVF cycles where embryo chromosomal status was controlled by transferring only euploid embryos. It found that greater vaginal microbial diversity and specific features of the CST-IV community state type were associated with pregnancy outcomes, suggesting the microbiome's effect is independent of embryo aneuploidy. The work refines prior conflicting findings by removing a major confounder.

papers.title: Effects of trait stacking on the maize phyllosphere microbiome: a shotgun metagenomic comparison.
papers.abstract: Current safety assessments for stacked-trait transgenic crops underrepresent the phyllosphere, a critical interface directly exposed to transgenic products, warranting strengthened risk evaluation. Here, we employed metagenomics to characterize the phyllosphere of three maize lines under herbicide-free conditions: wild-type (Corn.CK), herbicide-resistant single-trait (transgene of cp4-epsps, Corn.S), and insect- and herbicide-resistant stacked-trait (transgene of cry1Ab and cp4-epsps, Corn.D). Shannon diversity showed a consistent trend toward higher values in the cp4-epsps single-trait line t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the phyllosphere microbiome of three maize lines: wild-type, a single-trait herbicide-resistant line (cp4-epsps), and a stacked-trait line (cry1Ab + cp4-epsps), all grown without herbicide. Shannon diversity trended higher in the single-trait line, suggesting that trait stacking may influence the leaf-surface microbial community, though the abstract is truncated and full conclusions are unclear. The work argues that phyllosphere communities should be included in safety assessments of stacked transgenic crops.

papers.title: CRC-TrustBench: benchmarking cross-study and cross-country generalization in gut metagenomic colorectal cancer prediction.
papers.abstract: Gut metagenomic classifiers for colorectal cancer (CRC) are often evaluated with random splits that place samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, potentially inflating apparent performance. We developed CRC-TrustBench, a leakage-aware framework for evaluating cross-study and cross-country generalization and probability reliability.
papers.summary: CRC-TrustBench is a leakage-aware benchmarking framework that evaluates gut metagenomic colorectal cancer classifiers under cross-study and cross-country generalization rather than random splits. It shows that conventional random splits can inflate apparent performance by placing samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, and it adds assessment of probability reliability.

papers.title: A genome-resolved cyanobacterial consortium from the Atacama Desert reveals novel bacterial diversity, stress-resilience potential, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection.
papers.abstract: The Atacama Desert is one of the most extreme terrestrial environments on Earth, characterized by hyper-aridity, intense solar and ultraviolet radiation, oxidative stress, and metal-rich substrates. Here, we characterized an enriched cyanobacteria-associated consortium obtained from a high-altitude, river-influenced site in Quebrada Talabre, Atacama Desert. Deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing, achieving 99.7% estimated community coverage, enabled the reconstruction of 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes representing five bacterial phyla. Genome-resolved analyses revealed multiple puta
papers.summary: The authors enriched a cyanobacteria-associated microbial community from a high-altitude site in the Atacama Desert and used deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing to reconstruct 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes spanning five bacterial phyla. Genome-resolved analyses uncovered novel bacterial diversity and genes suggesting stress resilience, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection mechanisms adapted to extreme solar radiation and hyper-aridity.

papers.title: Cervico-vaginal microbiota and antimicrobial resistance patterns in relation to different reproductive statuses in cattle: a field study from Nepal.
papers.abstract: Vaginal bacterial communities are increasingly recognized as key determinants of fertility in cattle. This study explored bacterial communities in the cervico-vaginal mucus of healthy heifers, cows with cervicitis, repeat-breeding, and cows within the 35-day postpartum period using the microbiological culture method (n=35) and sequencing of the V3-V4 hypervariable regions of 16S rRNA gene (n=18), along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Micrococcus spp. and Enterobacter spp. were the top two bacteria isolated across the groups. Alarmingly, antimicrobial sensitivity tests revealed a hig
papers.summary: This field study from Nepal characterized cervico-vaginal bacterial communities in cattle across different reproductive statuses—healthy heifers, cows with cervicitis, repeat-breeding cows, and postpartum cows—using culture and 16S rRNA sequencing. Micrococcus and Enterobacter were the most common isolates, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed alarmingly high resistance rates. The work highlights both the microbial diversity associated with reproductive disorders and a concerning antimicrobial resistance burden in livestock reproductive tract infections.

papers.title: Oliceridine and morphine differentially modulate the gut microbiota-intestinal barrier axis in a rat postoperative pain model.
papers.abstract: Oliceridine is a novel G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist with potentially improved gastrointestinal tolerability compared with conventional opioids. However, its impact on postoperative intestinal homeostasis-specifically the gut microbiota and intestinal barrier-remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study compares oliceridine, a G protein-biased mu-opioid agonist, with morphine in a rat postoperative pain model, focusing on effects on gut microbiota composition and intestinal barrier integrity. The authors report that the two opioids differentially modulate the microbiota–barrier axis, suggesting oliceridine may have a distinct gastrointestinal profile. The work is preliminary (abstract-only) but points to a potential tolerability advantage worth follow-up.

papers.title: Dynamic changes in gut microbiota of three breeds of stud boars pre- and post-amoxicillin administration.
papers.abstract: Amoxicillin is a commonly used broad-spectrum antibiotic in pig farming, valued for its cost-effectiveness and efficacy in addressing prevalent swine ailments. However, the specific effects on the gut microbiota of stud boars and the trajectory of microbial recovery post-antibiotic withdrawal remain insufficiently elucidated.
papers.summary: This study tracked changes in the gut microbiota of three breeds of stud boars before and after amoxicillin administration, examining how the microbial community is disrupted and how it recovers after the antibiotic is withdrawn. It provides breed-specific insight into antibiotic-induced dysbiosis in an understudied livestock population.

papers.title: Prebiotic dietary fibers, gut microbiota, and short-chain fatty acid production: from fermentation mechanisms to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: The importance of the gut microbiota in regulating host homeostasis, immune responses, metabolism, and dietary interactions is increasingly recognized. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), microbial metabolites produced through the fermentation of dietary substrates, play a central role in mediating these interactions. Drawing on mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and insights from in vitro host-microbe fermentation models, this review critically examines how prebiotic dietary fibers have influenced the human gut microbial ecosystem, fermentation pathways, and SCFA production over the past
papers.summary: This review examines how prebiotic dietary fibers shape the gut microbial ecosystem and drive short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production through fermentation. It synthesizes mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and in vitro host-microbe fermentation models, and discusses pathways toward clinical translation of these findings. The work highlights SCFAs as central mediators of diet-microbe-host interactions affecting metabolism, immunity, and homeostasis.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform for microbiome research that aims to unify fragmented microbial data, heterogeneous knowledge representations, and analytical tools. The authors argue that existing databases and knowledge graphs are too narrowly focused on genomic information, neglecting metabolomic and literature-derived associations, and propose IMicAP as a knowledge-driven solution to bridge these gaps.

papers.title: Potential involvement of a TLR4-associated CD155/TIGIT pathway in Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced immunosuppressive microenvironment formation in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis may promote an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in oral squamous cell carcinoma. The authors propose that P. gingivalis activates a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling axis, which could suppress anti-tumor immune responses and thereby support cancer progression. The work links oral microbiome dysbiosis to immune evasion mechanisms in OSCC.

papers.title: Modulation of microbiota by traditional Chinese medicine in chronic inflammatory airway disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of animal studies.
papers.abstract: A growing number of studies have indicated that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can regulate microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway disease (CIAD). Nevertheless, no systematic review or integrated analysis has summarized relevant evidence to date, limiting the clinical application of TCM in this field.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence from animal studies on how traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) modulates the microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway diseases. It is the first integrated analysis of this topic, aiming to support the clinical application of TCM by consolidating preclinical findings.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tongue-image analysis may provide an objective, low-cost, and non-invasive adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines whether artificial intelligence applied to tongue images can serve as a non-invasive screening tool for gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders. It frames AI tongue-image analysis as a potential low-cost adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification, addressing the invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy.
